title: Maple Street, Curtis Crossing looking south
description: Collision at Maple Street Crossing, July 7, 1905: On a Monday morning in Hartland, the up freight train hauled by Engine No. 170 was standing in the yard when it was struck head-on by the southbound Plaster Rock train. The crash left both engines almost fit for the scrap heap. Passengers on the Plaster Rock train were badly shaken. A. J. McLean of Bristol suffered some bruises. Burke of Johnville and his daughter, en route to Debec, were thrown from their seats by the sudden jolt. The young woman was thrown against the stove, loosening several teeth and dislocating her wrist. Dr. Curtis tended to her injuries. Superintendent Newcomb, with a wrecking crew, cleared the track within a few hours. An investigation was launched to determine responsibility for the accident. Local officials reportedly settled with those who suffered damages.
